source.title: Accelerate Scaling of LLM Finetuning via Quantifying the Coverage and Depth of Instruction Set
source.authors: Cheng-Wei Wu; Li Du; Han-Yu Zhao; Yi-Ming Ju; Jia-Pu Wang; Tian-Yu Chen; Hao-Yi Zhou

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses scaling in supervised fine-tuning and cites the original pretraining scaling-law papers, but does not test their power laws, extrapolations, compute-optimal allocations, architecture effects, or fit dependence.
record.gate_note: The paper's experiments vary instruction-set selection, coverage, depth, and size during SFT. They do not sweep model parameters, pretraining tokens, or training compute; fit or test power laws in those variables; or test compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. The SFT loss and downstream-score results below are adjacent findings, not measurements of the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study is about SFT data selection. It regresses SFT dev loss on instruction-set coverage and relative depth, and compares ILA with random and Deita selection. It never fits loss against parameters, pretraining tokens or compute. It never tests extrapolation, compute-optimal splits, architecture shape, or whether downstream scores are predictable from scale. Kaplan and Hoffmann are cited only to motivate 'informational sufficiency'. Appendix B varies model size (1.5B/3B/7B) but fits no law, so it is not a test of V5 or V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that instruction-set coverage and information depth are significantly related to fine-tuned performance. They also conclude that ILA, which maximises both, outperforms the random and Deita baselines and makes SFT scaling more efficient and sustained ('accelerated scaling').
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates instruction-set properties and data-selection methods during SFT, rather than reproducing pretraining scaling-law experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports outcomes varying with instruction-set selection method, subset size, model, and evaluation benchmark; these are not tests of the claimed pretraining-law setup choices.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 36 SFT subsets, log dev loss regressed on log relative depth and log coverage explains over 70% of the variance. Both coefficients are negative.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SFT dev loss follows a log-linear relation with instruction-set coverage and relative information depth.

fits_no_version.finding: ILA beats random selection on MATH at 20k, 50k and 100k. Random selection stagnates from 50k to 100k (0.5914 to 0.5864).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under random selection, SFT gains on math stall as the instruction count grows. Coverage- and depth-aware selection sustains the gains.

fits_no_version.finding: With ILA subsets, AlpacaEval 2.0 scores rise with subset size (10k to 50k) and with model size (1.5B to 7B).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SFT downstream scores rise with instruction count and model size under ILA selection.

record.problems: The study does not test the listed scaling-law claims. For the adjacent SFT findings, reported results generally lack uncertainty measures; several comparisons are described in figures without per-condition values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's qualitative Figure 4 comparisons among ILA, random selection, Deita, and full-pool training, and the Figure 5 indicator comparisons, were not given separate rows because the text does not provide per-condition numerical values and they are SFT selection results rather than tests of the listed versions.

untested.parts: No sweep of held-out pretraining loss over parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No fixed-compute allocation of parameters versus tokens.
No depth or width comparison at a fixed parameter count.
Has SFT experiments, but fits no power law of SFT loss in data size, model size or compute.
Downstream scores are reported at three model sizes, but there is no test of predictability from scale or from pretraining loss.
No comparison of exponents or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: 'Scaling' here means returns to SFT data size, not pretraining scaling laws. The paper reports no uncertainty. The Figure 4 and Figure 5 results give no per-condition numbers in the text.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining-loss sweep over parameter count, tokens, or compute.
No extrapolation from small pretraining runs to larger runs.
No fixed-compute comparison of parameter/token allocations.
No comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The study conducts SFT experiments, but does not test whether the same power-law form holds in fine-tuning or other training regimes.
The study evaluates downstream scores after SFT, but does not test their predictability from model scale or pretraining loss.
No comparison of pretraining-law exponents or compute-optimal splits under different fitting or setup choices.

rows.subject: finetuned base LLM (not named)
rows.operation_detail: Regressed development cross-entropy loss on instruction-set relative information depth and coverage across 36 datasets.
rows.measure: development-set mean cross-entropy loss; regression explained over 70% of its variance, with both coefficients described as highly statistically significant and negative
rows.uncertainty: Statistical significance is stated; p-value or other uncertainty measure not stated.
rows.note: This is an SFT loss result against data properties, not a power-law fit against parameters, tokens, or compute.
rows.check: The subject is not named for the regression fine-tunes. Llama3-8B is the named base model used to estimate information depth. The fit (Eq. 6) is log-log linear in relative depth and coverage, not in N, D or C, so it is not a V1 or V5 power-law test.
